variants.name: JPA association with fetch = LAZY (provider-generated proxy)
variants.implementation_notes: The JPA standard absorbs the pattern: FetchType.LAZY is a hint the provider satisfies by handing back a proxy or deferred handle, and Hibernate implements it as a subclass proxy driven by LazyInitializer that loads the entity on the first non-identifier access. Collections (@OneToMany, @ManyToMany) default to LAZY while @ManyToOne/@OneToOne default to EAGER, so the association declarations are where the policy is written; EntityManager.getReference is the explicit form when only the reference is needed.
pitfalls: Accessing a lazy association outside the persistence context throws LazyInitializationException; open-session-in-view hides that by keeping the session (and its connection) alive for the whole request.
@ManyToOne and @OneToOne default to EAGER, so a naive graph drags the world in: set fetch = LAZY explicitly and prefetch what a use case needs with join fetch or an EntityGraph.

Provider proxies are subclasses: getClass(), instanceof and equals/hashCode over concrete types misbehave on an uninitialized proxy - compare identifiers, and keep entities non-final with a no-arg constructor.

variants.name: Volatile double-checked holder (or memoized Supplier)
variants.implementation_notes: Outside a provider the holder is hand-written: a volatile field plus the synchronized double-check - volatile is what makes the idiom correct under the Java memory model - or a Supplier<T> wrapped by a memoizing holder such as Guava's Suppliers.memoize. Choose it for DTOs, non-JPA stores (JDBC, HTTP clients) or when the loaded value must not be a provider proxy, because the explicit form also lets you choose whether a failure is cached or retried.
variants.idiom_name: volatile field + synchronized double-check, or Suppliers.memoize
pitfalls: Dropping volatile (or reading the fast path outside the synchronized block for the second check) reintroduces the broken double-checked locking idiom: two threads can build two different authors.
A null field cannot distinguish 'not loaded' from 'author absent', so absent rows re-query forever; use a sentinel or a loaded flag.
Holding the monitor while the loader performs a database call blocks every other synchronized method of the same object.
